diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Assume $\widehat b_{i,k}(s)=b_{i,k}(s)$ for all $s\in\mathcal F$ and that  $
\max_{s\in\mathcal T}\max_{(i,k)\in\mathcal I}\big|\widehat b_{i,k}(s)-b_{i,k}(s)\big|
\le
\varepsilon_b.$

\widehat\gamma
:=
\gamma + C_{{\mathrm q},\infty}N\varepsilon_b\,C_{\infty,{\mathrm q}}.
\end{equation}
Assume $\varepsilon_b$ is chosen so that $\widehat\gamma<1$.
Assume the structural learning and weight estimation steps succeed and assume $\widehat\gamma<1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts that the learned projected operator is contractive on the anchored subspace under only the conditions of Lemma lem:main_Pihat_dev (anchor exactness on recurrent states and a uniform weight error $\varepsilon_b$ on transient states). However, the contraction factor is $\widehat\gamma=\gamma+C_{q,\infty}C_{\infty,q}N\varepsilon_b$, which is $<1$ only when $\varepsilon_b<(1-\gamma)/(C_{q,\infty}C_{\infty,q}N)$. The stated conditions allow $\varepsilon_b\in(0,1)$ arbitrarily close to $1$ (and $N$ large), in which case $\widehat\gamma>1$ and the operator is not a contraction. The claim 'is contractive' therefore omits the necessary smallness hypothesis on $\varepsilon_b$ (equivalently $\widehat\gamma<1$). The formal template Lemma lem:projSA_stability_template and the main rate Theorem thm:main_sa_rate both impose $\widehat\gamma<1$ explicitly, so the main results are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\varepsilon_b$ is small enough that $\widehat\gamma=\gamma+O(N\varepsilon_b)<1$ (equivalently, assume $\widehat\gamma<1$), matching the formal version Lemma lem:projSA_stability_template and the assumption in Theorem thm:main_sa_rate.
issues.overall_effect: Only the informal main-text statement of Lemma lem:main_hat_contraction overclaims. The main convergence theorem thm:main_sa_rate and the formal template lem:projSA_stability_template already assume $\widehat\gamma<1$, so no downstream rate, guarantee, or dependent result is invalidated.
issues.title: Contraction lemma asserts contractivity without the smallness hypothesis on the weight error
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line addition of the smallness hypothesis, which the main theorem already assumes; the method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope all survive, and no new argument is required.
